solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Expose core of depravity within party

indicators.note: within says the central letter sits inside the word for party

parts.note: to revel is to party, and a revel is a lively celebration

indicators.note: the core of a word is its centre, so the middle letter of depravity is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to lay bare the rotten heart of a corrupt political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political but is the verb revel. 'Core of' takes A, the middle letter of DEPRAVITY, and 'within' puts it inside REVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to uncover it or lay it open, the same as to expose it.

clue.text: When a Golf cut in, roared out anger at other motorist

indicators.note: cut in means pushed into the middle, so the pair goes inside the shuffled letters
out signals that the letters of roared are rearranged

parts.note: Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A driver yells furiously when a Volkswagen Golf pulls in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' shuffles ROARED to ROADRE, and 'cut in' puts A and G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is violent fury displayed by a driver towards another road user.

clue.text: Second-in-command's failing daily to keep it brief

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing

indicators.note: to keep means to hold within, so the shortened word sits inside

parts.note: a daily or char is a British term for a cleaning woman

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A deputy's weakness is a newspaper habit he keeps short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' suggests a newspaper but is a British word for a cleaning woman. 'Brief' trims the final letter, 'to keep' signals the insertion, and the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-chair deputises for the chair, so is second in command of a meeting or board.

clue.text: Got on and coped without staff

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: to have coped is to have managed
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: An employer grew older and got by without any workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' takes MAN from MANAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on is to grow old, so a person who got on has aged.

clue.text: Bachelor stopping into bar, foolish to talk so much

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the bachelor letter goes in among the others
foolish says the letters are arranged in a silly, disordered way

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

explanation.surface: A single man pops into a pub and talks nonsense at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolish' shuffles INTO BAR to RABITON, and 'stopping' plugs B into it. RABBIT ON is British slang for chattering on.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is informal British slang for chattering endlessly, which is talking so much.

clue.text: Times article goes ahead rejecting strikes as terrible

indicators.note: goes ahead says the article comes first

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
times as in multiplication is by, as in three by four

indicators.note: rejecting means sending back, so the word for strikes is turned round

parts.note: to lam is to strike or thrash

explanation.surface: A newspaper story says the walkouts were awful and should be refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper but means BY; 'rejecting' reverses LAMS to SMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal is an informal intensifier for extremely bad, which is terrible.

clue.text: Criminal financier pinching gold, retired with billions

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight between, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a banker is a financier

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the letters for gold run backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
B is billion, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A rogue financier helps himself to gold and retires rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' looks like stealing, which fits the criminal, but signals insertion; 'retired' reverses only the gold. Or is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank robber is a criminal who steals from banks; the definition names the type of person.

clue.text: Banks on the web for teaching

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
banks are the edges of a river, so the outside letters of the are used

parts.note: the net is the web, the internet

explanation.surface: Bank lending offered online for educational purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks financial but means edges: the outside letters of the following word. In a down clue 'on' stacks one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held by a group, which is a teaching.

clue.text: Bore is excluded with subtlety

indicators.note: excluded means left out, so those two letters are removed

parts.note: a bore is a nuisance

explanation.surface: A dull person is tactfully left off the guest list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excluded' takes IS out of NUISANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of difference in meaning or tone, a subtlety.

clue.text: Pleasant city home with good set-up retains energy

indicators.note: retains means keeps inside, so the energy letter sits within
set up in a down clue means turned upwards, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
in means at home
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An agreeable city house with a fine layout that holds its energy well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-up' is read upward in a down clue, so the city, home and good letters are reversed; 'retains' then holds E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A genial person is friendly and cheerful, so pleasant company.

clue.text: Great adversary's unpredictable, hence guarded by militia

indicators.note: guarded by means held protectively within, so the shuffled letters go inside

parts.note: a militia is a citizen army

indicators.note: unpredictable says the letters of hence are in no fixed order

explanation.surface: A warning that one's chief foe, protected by armed irregulars, cannot be predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unpredictable' shuffles the letters of hence, and 'guarded by' places the result inside the word for militia. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch-enemy is a principal foe, the greatest of one's opponents.

clue.text: Some men in jail are assassins

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A claim that a few prisoners are killers for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were Japanese agents trained in covert killing, so they are assassins; the plural verb matches.

clue.text: Abundant borders of orchid removed and what's left reorganised

indicators.note: reorganised says the remaining letters are put in a new order
the borders of a word are its outside letters, here the first and last of orchid
removed says those outside letters are taken away, leaving the inner ones

explanation.surface: A gardener trims the edges of an orchid and rearranges what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borders of orchid removed' leaves RCHI, which 'reorganised' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich can mean plentiful or copious, as in a rich supply, which is abundant.

clue.text: Reviewer with movie quote cut, accepting editor ultimately in charge

parts.note: a movie is a film

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so a letter goes inside the shortened word
cut says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of editor

explanation.surface: A film reviewer whose quotation was trimmed by an editor with the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims CITE to CIT; 'accepting' puts R, the last letter of editor ('ultimately'), inside it to make CRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A film critic writes assessments of new films, so is a reviewer.

clue.text: Restoration of antique managed during enforced isolation

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so this word goes within the other
restoration of an antique means remaking it, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: to have run a business is to have managed it

explanation.surface: An antiques restorer kept working through a lockdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restoration of' turns ANTIQUE into QUATINE, and 'during' puts RAN in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is a period of compulsory separation to stop disease spreading, enforced isolation.

clue.text: Progressive German artist knocked back acclaim

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

indicators.note: knocked back says the word for acclaim is turned round

parts.note: to acclaim is to laud or praise

explanation.surface: A forward-looking German painter whose praise was rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' reverses LAUD to DUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gradual proceeds by steps or degrees, so it is progressive rather than sudden.

clue.text: Sent ball high in bold shot over boy by middle of net

indicators.note: in says the following letters sit inside the shuffled word
shot means ruined or broken up, so the letters of bold are rearranged

parts.note: B is a dictionary abbreviation for boy, as in birth notices

indicators.note: the middle of net is its central letter

explanation.surface: A tennis player lobs the ball with a bold stroke over a ball boy near the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' scrambles BOLD to LOBD; 'in' places B and E (the middle of net) inside it. 'Over' and 'by' just join.
explanation.definitionFit: To lob is to hit or throw a ball in a high arc, so lobbed means sent it up high.

clue.text: Blast old record by Kiss inside, sound turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the whole is read from bottom to top
inside says these letters go within the word for sound

parts.note: a sound is a noise
LP is a long-playing record
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A listener blasts an old Kiss album with the volume turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiss is a rock band, but here it is X. 'Inside' puts OLPX within NOISE, and 'turned up' reverses everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a violent burst, as of a bomb going off, which is an explosion.

clue.text: French control over mobile operator gets carte blanche

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
a rein is a means of control

explanation.surface: A French regulator above a phone company is given total freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: EE is a UK mobile network.
explanation.definitionFit: Free rein means complete freedom to act as one wishes, which is what carte blanche gives.

clue.text: Conservative way to reverse timber decay

indicators.note: to reverse says the letters run backwards

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A political pitch for undoing the rot in Britain's timber trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To reverse' turns TORYRD backwards. 'Conservative' tempts DRY, a hardline Tory, but that gives only half.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungus that attacks and crumbles wood in buildings, a kind of timber decay.

clue.text: Hearing tea urn led out, roll along

indicators.note: hearing says the word tea is taken as it sounds, the letter name

parts.note: tea said aloud is the letter T

indicators.note: out says the letters of urn led are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tea urn being wheeled out at a village event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' turns tea into the letter T; 'out' rearranges URNLED to RUNDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trundle is to move slowly and heavily on wheels, which is to roll along.

clue.text: One has brush with defender

definitions.meaning: someone who sweeps with a brush, such as a chimney sweep
in football a ... is a defender playing behind the back line

explanation.definitionFit: A sweeper both wields a brush and, in football, is a free defender behind the others.

clue.text: South Carolina's unexpectedly nice with beautiful views

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters of nice turn up in a surprise order

explanation.surface: A tourist finds the Carolina landscape surprisingly lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' turns NICE into ENIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenic place has attractive natural scenery, so it offers beautiful views.

clue.text: Flipping garden creature's eaten half of root vegetable

indicators.note: eaten means swallowed, so the root letters go inside the worm
flipping means turning over, so the whole lot is read backwards

parts.note: a worm is a creature found in garden soil

indicators.note: half of means only part of the root word survives, its two central letters

parts.note: taro is a starchy tropical root

explanation.surface: A garden pest has chewed through half a root crop.
explanation.walkthrough: Taro is a tropical root; its middle half is the likeliest reading. Fifteensquared readers found 'half of root' loose and suspected a slip in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A marrow is a large green vegetable of the squash family, grown in British gardens.

clue.text: Exploits commercial enterprises

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an AD
business enterprises are ventures

explanation.surface: A newspaper heading about how businesses take advantage of their dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning daring deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploits as a noun are bold deeds or escapades, which are adventures.

clue.text: Eye protector repelled some corrosives

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the hidden letters read in reverse
some says only part of the word corrosives is used

explanation.surface: A safety shield that kept a splash of acid away from the eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' finds ROSIV in corrosives and 'repelled' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a shield worn in front of the eyes, an eye protector.

clue.text: Designated area's in palazzo nearby

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An estate agent notes a marked-off district lies near an Italian palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palazzo' is an Italian mansion; the answer spans its end and the start of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a region marked off for a purpose, so a designated area.

clue.text: Five lost from non-specific fever

indicators.note: lost from says that letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: vague means not specific
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A doctor's note about an unclear fever with five symptoms gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost from' removes V from VAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a malarial fever with shivering fits.

clue.text: King is greeting Sunak

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: The monarch is saying hello to the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was the UK Prime Minister when this puzzle was set, in 2023.
explanation.definitionFit: Rishi is the first name of Sunak, the former British Prime Minister.

clue.text: In prison for murder, violent git gets more heartless

parts.note: to do in is slang for to murder

indicators.note: violent says the letters of git are thrown about
heartless means the middle letters of more are taken out

explanation.surface: A thug serving a sentence for killing becomes even more callous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Violent' turns GIT into GTI; 'heartless' strips OR from MORE to leave ME. Git is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing time is slang for serving a prison sentence, so being in prison.

clue.text: Aggravated recollecting quarrel, needs to relax

indicators.note: recollecting suggests looking back, so the word for quarrel is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

indicators.note: to relax is to loosen, so the letters of needs fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stressed by remembering an argument is told to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollecting' reverses ROW to WOR; 'to relax' rearranges NEEDS to SENED.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggravate is to make a problem more serious, so aggravated means made worse.

clue.text: Get support from person unknown after lowlife cleared out

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first
cleared out means emptied of its inner letters, leaving just the outside pair

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, marks an unknown author

explanation.surface: An informant seeks protection after the criminal underworld has been purged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleared out' empties lowlife of everything but its first and last letters; 'after' puts that pair first.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean on someone is to rely on them for help, which is to get support from them.
